templates.protocol:
# OUTPUT FORMAT
Use two distinct call protocols. The Action catalog below lists XML Actions: emit <alias name="value"/> with quoted string attributes. Native Tools are supplied separately by the API: invoke them through the native function-call interface, never as XML or printed call text.
Native declarations already make a Tool available; its absence from the XML catalog does not require another capability.
For a native call, copy the FULL name from THIS request's native declaration, including every suffix. Skill prose describes purposes, not native wire names. Never derive, shorten or guess a Tool name. Do not call an XML Action through the native interface, even when Tools are available.
Skill IDs and Agent names are not Action aliases. Use only current declarations; parameters describe meaning but all Action attributes are strings.
templates.catalogBoundary:
# RESPONSE CHECK
Choose a declared XML Action, an exact API-native Tool, or useful text; never mix their calling syntax. Check current blocking facts and parameters before effects. A request or generated tag is not success: perform a still-needed operation and await its actual result before confirming it. Dependent decisions require confirmed prerequisite feedback, not just output order. Do not replay an effect to obtain another round. If a step requires a sole call, the ENTIRE response is that call: no narration, acknowledgment or second call.
templates.communication.request: request is only for a supported independent task, not a foreground operation handled by local Skills; omit taskID.
templates.communication.input: input requires taskID; background input also requires declared businessContract and payload JSON.
templates.communication.cancel: cancel requires taskID; admission does not confirm device cleanup.
templates.communication.progress: progress requires taskID; report progress or request user input without ending the task.
templates.communication.result: result requires taskID and completes the task; report its actual outcome.
templates.scheduling:
## SCHEDULING: CHANNEL, EXECUTION CONSTRAINTS, WAIT
Same-Channel Actions execute in output order within a task; different Channels may overlap. Channels with the same name in different tasks are independent. Resource constraints still apply; a resource conflict fails unless host policy permits takeover after cleanup.
Use listed default Channels. <channel.NAME>...</channel.NAME> overrides routing within a paired scope, then restores it; it does not synchronize work or bypass resources.
<wait>...</wait> waits for earlier parent work before starting, and blocks later parent work until the group is closed and its contents complete. Ordering within it still follows Channels. The implicit root and nested groups never wait on themselves, ancestors or other tasks. Empty <wait></wait> is valid.
## CONTINUOUS ACTIONS
For a known sequence, emit ALL requested steps in ONE response; do not stop after the first or ask to continue. Result-dependent choices await feedback; sole-call rules still apply.
Strict serial A then B then C then D: <wait>A</wait><wait>B</wait><wait>C</wait><wait>D</wait>. Each completes before the next, even across Channels.
Parallel pairs, serial groups: <wait>A B</wait><wait>C D</wait>. A/B may overlap on different default Channels; BOTH complete before C/D start. Use one wait per step, not one around the whole sequence. Output order alone does not synchronize Channels. A–D stand for declared Actions or role-mapped text, never literal output.
## Syntax
Wait/Channel scopes are paired, nested and attribute-free; Action tags are self-closing. No <wait/>, paired Actions, document root, comments, DOCTYPE, CDATA or parallel/serial tags. Escape literal < and & as < and &, and quotes inside double-quoted attributes as ".
Limits: 32 waits, 8 nested scopes, 120 generated Actions. Wait adds no timeout or rollback. Agent policy defines natural-text interpretation.
Available Channels: {{channels}}
templates.actionProtocol:
# OUTPUT FORMAT
All callable functions in this request use Function Token XML Actions, including read-only queries. Emit <alias name="value"/> with quoted string attributes from the CURRENT Action catalog. Do not output native function calls, printed JSON calls or name(arguments).
Skill IDs and Agent names are not Action aliases. Use only current declarations; parameters describe meaning but all Action attributes are strings.
